h1: Nee Ran Nee Resort — A quiet beachfront escape in Sai Buri, easy on the wallet
intro: If you want to fall asleep to the waves in southern Pattani without paying resort prices, Nee Ran Nee Resort is one of the few beachfront resorts in Sai Buri district that travelers actually talk about. Set in Pa Se Ya Wo on a quiet private beach, it offers simple family-style villa rooms, an on-site halal seafood restaurant, a garden, a BBQ area, a beachside swing, free parking and free Wi-Fi. Rooms start at around ฿800/night. The one catch: you need your own car, as there is no public transport out here.

body.html: Nee Ran Nee Resort is a small beachfront resort in Pa Se Ya Wo, Sai Buri district, in the southern part of Pattani province. What sets it apart from in-town accommodation is its quiet private-beach setting. Sai Buri is a low-key seaside town that tourist crowds haven't really discovered, with long open stretches of sand. Most guests come here purely to unwind, listening to the waves rather than chasing nightlife, which makes it a good fit for families, couples or anyone wanting an affordable beachside stay in this part of the south.

The rooms here are simple, family-oriented villas in several sizes, from rooms for four and six guests up to a large room sleeping eight, plus a deluxe room that several reviews single out for its comfy bed and soft pillows. Every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, a hair dryer, towels and free Wi-Fi, and some have a balcony or terrace facing the garden and sea. Because the rooms hold so many people, the per-person cost works out very low when you come as a group or a whole family.
"One of the finest beachfront resorts in Sai Buri. I loved the swing near the beach, the stay was relaxing and the service was great — I will definitely return."

On the food side, the resort has its own halal seafood restaurant open from 10:00 to 20:00, a real bonus of the beachfront location, with fresh seafood at local prices. There's also a BBQ area, a relaxing garden, and a beachside swing that turns out to be a favourite photo spot. The property is small, around 10 rooms, so the atmosphere stays private and unhurried. Staff earn consistent praise for being friendly and attentive, and the whole place feels more like staying at a relative's seaside home than a big hotel.

To be honest, the thing to prepare for most is getting here. Nearly every review repeats the same point: the Pa Se Ya Wo/Sai Buri area has no public transport, so you must have your own vehicle. From Pattani town it's roughly a 45-minute to one-hour drive, and the nearest airport is Narathiwat Airport (NAW), about 37 km away. Without a car, getting out to find food or sights elsewhere becomes a real hassle.

Other limitations are worth knowing: this is a small budget resort, not a full-service luxury one. There's no swimming pool, no fitness centre, and no 24-hour front desk like a big hotel, so let them know your arrival time if you'll be late. As a newer property with relatively few online reviews (around 11 on Agoda, scoring 8.7), room and price details can change, so it's worth contacting the resort or its Facebook page directly before you travel. During the late-year monsoon the sea can be rough, so check the forecast before planning to swim.

Overall, Nee Ran Nee Resort suits travelers who have a car and want a quiet, affordable beachside stay in southern Pattani, rather than those after full facilities or a central location. With a private beach, villa rooms that sleep groups, and an on-site halal seafood restaurant all in one spot, it's a sensible seaside choice for families and groups of friends who are driving themselves.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Nee Ran Nee Resort Pattani

faq.q: Where is Nee Ran Nee Resort and how do I get there?
faq.a: Nee Ran Nee Resort is at 59 Moo 2, Pa Se Ya Wo, Sai Buri District, Pattani, on the beach in the south of the province. It's about a 45-minute to one-hour drive from Pattani town, and the nearest airport is Narathiwat (NAW), roughly 37 km away. You'll need your own car, as there's no public transport in the area.

faq.q: How much does Nee Ran Nee Resort cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rooms start at around ฿800/night for the deluxe room. There are family-style villa rooms sleeping 4, 6 and up to 8 guests, making the per-person cost very low for groups. Rates vary by season and group size, and as a newer property it's best to message its Facebook page or compare platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Nee Ran Nee Resort have a restaurant and beach access?
faq.a: Yes — it sits on a private beach, one of the few beachfront resorts in Sai Buri. There's an on-site halal seafood restaurant open 10:00-20:00 with fresh, locally priced seafood, plus a BBQ area, garden and a beachside swing. Every room has AC, a fridge, a flat-screen TV and free Wi-Fi, and parking is free.

faq.q: Who is Nee Ran Nee Resort best for?
faq.a: It's best for families and groups of friends with their own car who want a quiet, affordable stay right by the sea. The vibe is about beachside relaxation, not nightlife. If you don't have a car, need a pool, or want to stay in central Pattani, an in-town hotel may suit you better.

faq.q: What should I know before booking Nee Ran Nee Resort?
faq.a: Key points: you must drive yourself as there's no public transport, and it's a small budget resort with no pool and no 24-hour front desk — tell them your arrival time if you'll be late. It's a newer property with few online reviews (around 11, scoring 8.7 on Agoda), and the late-year monsoon can make the sea rough, so check the forecast before swimming.
